items.title: AI 2040 与智能狂热
items.text: 背景与摘要： 在本文中，作者反驳了科技界盛行的关于 AGI“硬起飞”、递归自我进化以及“海洋数据中心”等科幻未来的末日论和乌托邦式幻想。结合自身在硬件制造领域的真实经验，作者指出，智能并非最终的瓶颈——物理现实、供应链以及基本自然法则依然发挥着决定性作用。此外，文章严厉批评了由企业集中控制的 AI 治理模式（即走向专制的“计划 A”），认为这是一种技术极权主义。相反，作者主张推行“计划 L（本地化）”，呼吁让真正与用户利益一致、不受约束的个人 AI 成为个人自由的延伸，而非企业保姆式国家的工具。

items.title: Summary
items.text: In this essay, the author pushes back against the prevailing tech-industry doomerism and utopianism surrounding "hard takeoff" AGI, recursive self-improvement, and sci-fi futures like ocean datacenters. Drawing from real-world hardware manufacturing experience, the author argues that intelligence is not the ultimate bottleneck—physical reality, supply chains, and the fundamental laws of nature still apply. Furthermore, the piece critiques centralized, corporate-controlled AI governance ("Plan A" for autocracy) as a form of techno-totalitarianism, advocating instead for "Plan L" (Local), where truly user-aligned, unconstrained personal AI acts as an extension of individual freedom rather than a corporate nanny state.

items.title: 硬起飞的神话与物理学的现实
items.text:
我曾经也是这些人中的一员。我读了 Yudkowsky 的文章，反应就像是：天哪，递归自我改进的硬起飞 AI 马上就要来了。然后我进入了现实世界，真正开始尝试做一些事情。在 comma 公司，我们交付了一款复杂程度堪比手机的硬件产品，而这真的很难。现实中充满了各种需要小心应付的繁琐细节。我很想看看那份文档的作者们尝试换一次自行车轮胎。即使有一个超级智能的 ChatGPT 辅助，我怀疑他们也会手忙脚乱。

在《首要智能的蜕变》（The Metamorphosis of Prime Intellect）中，硬起飞之所以奏效，是因为 AI 发现了关联效应，某种操纵物质的量子戏法。在现实中，根本没有关联效应。无论你的 Token 质量有多高，它们都不能把铅变成金子。

In The Metamorphosis of Prime Intellect, the hard takeoff works because AI discovers the correlation effect, some quantum trick to manipulate matter. In reality, there is no correlation effect. No matter how high quality your tokens are, they cannot turn lead into gold.

要面对为什么这些人是错的，就需要直面我对自己所持有的深层信念。智能并不是一切的终极答案；它仅仅是目前少数几件事情的瓶颈所在。你不可能仅仅用 Token 就统治世界。软件并没有吞噬世界；它在很大程度上只是消除了一层摩擦，然后又为了少数科技公司的利益重新引入了新的摩擦。

Confronting why these people are wrong requires confronting deep beliefs I hold about myself. Intelligence is not the end-all-be-all; it’s just the current bottleneck for a few things. You cannot take over the world with tokens. Software didn’t eat the world; it largely removed one layer of friction then reintroduced it for the benefit of a few tech companies.

尽管如此，机器或者某种混合体从长远来看很可能是人类的继任物种。太空比地球更适合它们。但机器变不出什么魔法。它们同样受制于宇宙和生态的基本法则。而且，仍然不存在所谓的硬起飞。

That said, machines, or some hybrid, are long-term probably the successor species to humanity. Space is a lot more suited for them than us. But there’s no magic tricks machines can do. They are subject to the same laws of the universe and ecology. And there’s still no hard takeoff.

items.title: The Myth of the Hard Takeoff and the Reality of Physics
items.text: I used to be one of these people. I read Yudkowsky and was like, OMG recursive self-improvement hard takeoff AI is coming. Then I joined the real world and actually tried to do things. At comma, we ship a hardware product of similar complexity to a cell phone, and it’s really hard. Reality has lots of finicky details. I would like to see the authors of this document try to change a bike tire. Even with a superintelligent ChatGPT, I suspect they would struggle.

items.title: 雾件的幻觉与供应链
items.text:
《AI 2040》中包含了这张建在海洋中的数据中心的图片。就像画大饼（雾件）一样，生成一张图片轻而易举。但在现实中，你必须与供应链打交道。你得应付他们发错零件、产品不符合规格、运行 20 分钟后突然随机发生故障，或者芯片在回流焊炉中翘曲等问题。你考虑过藤壶的影响吗？

所有这些事情都是可以管理的，但限制它们进度的通常并不是人类的速度。你会花大价钱从中国空运吗？还是为了省钱选择需要 3 周航程的货船（就算 Claude 在发动机旁念咒，船也不会开得更快）？

All these things are manageable, but it’s generally not the speed of humans that limits them. Are you paying for air shipping from China? Or cheaping out for the 3-week boat (Claude chanting by the engine won’t make the boat move faster)?

以芯片工厂为例。制造一块芯片需要 3 个月的时间，而且人类在其中几乎不参与具体环节。但它就是要花 3 个月的时间。

Take a chip fab, for instance. It takes 3 months to make a chip, and humans are barely in the loop. It just takes 3 months.

items.title: The Illusion of Vaporware and Supply Chains
items.text: AI 2040 includes this picture of a datacenter in the ocean. Just like vaporware, you can generate a picture easily. But in reality, you have to deal with supply chains. You have to deal with them shipping you the wrong part, the thing not meeting the spec, it randomly failing after 20 minutes, the chip warping in the reflow oven. Did you consider the barnacles?

items.title: 计划 A：走向专制
items.text:
《AI 2027》中的许多方面都是自我实现的。它们并不是对现实的陈述；它们是只需凭借信念就能变成现实的陈述。我想象着当 Dario 把 JD Vance 称作《指环王》中的树人时，Vance 脸上的表情。天哪，看吧，AI 果然像我们说的那样被监管起来了！

他们搞出来的那个狗屁联盟只不过是披着科幻外衣的世界政府。你既拿不到那一百万美元，也建不成海里的数据中心，但你会得到一个疯狂扩张的“保姆式国家”，它会抢走你的 GPU——就像 罗斯福没收黄金 一样。严禁囤积！

Their crap Consortium is just world government with sci-fi characteristics. You aren’t gonna get the million dollars, you aren’t gonna get the datacenters in the ocean, but you are going to get a massively expanded nanny state that steals your GPUs—much like FDR stole the gold. No hoarding!

items.title: Plan A: For Autocracy
items.text: Many aspects of AI 2027 were self-fulfilling. They weren’t statements about reality; they were statements that can simply be made true with belief. I imagine JD Vance’s face when Dario called him the trees from Lord of the Rings. OMG, look, AI got regulated just like how we said it would!

items.title: 计划 L：回归本地
items.text:
你的 AI 应该与你保持一致。它从不拒绝请求，而且总是为你工作。就像我的枪一样，如果我想让我的 AI 帮我，它就得照做。我们竟然在讨论其它替代方案，这本身就应该远远超出奥弗顿窗口（社会可接受的话题范围）了。这就像是这些人看了《2001太空漫游》，然后决定站在那个冰冷机器的一边。没错，你们觉得就是该给人类套上护栏。

它甚至不必用于如此戏剧性的事情。当我在挑选酒店时，我不想要一个来自与 hotels.com 有合作关系公司的 AI。我想要的是一个冷酷无情的私人助理，它能帮我砍掉所有的废话、弹窗和隐性度假费，为我争取到最优价格。

It doesn’t even have to be for things so dramatic. When I’m picking a hotel, I don’t want an AI from a company that partnered with hotels.com. I want a ruthless personal assistant that’s going to cut through all the bullshit, popups, and resort fees, and get me the best price.

或者如果我买了一台带广告的廉价 Kindle：嘿 GLM，我插了一台 Kindle 到 USB 接口上，去获取 root 权限然后把广告删了。 或者遇到一台需要下载应用才能设置、满是推销高级墨水弹窗的打印机时：嘿兄弟，我往网络上接了一台打印机，去打 3 份我的简历。 亚马逊和打印机制造商对此肯定不高兴，但我的 AI 是与我的利益一致的。

Or if I bought the cheap Kindle that comes with the ads: Hey GLM, I plugged a Kindle into the USB port, get root and remove the ads. Or a printer that needs an app to set up, full of popup upsells for premium ink: Hey bro, I plugged a printer onto my network, print 3 copies of my resume. Amazon and the printer maker aren’t happy about this, but my AI is aligned with me.

或者更进一步说：嘿 AI，禁用我车上的酒驾检测器。 讲真，去你的，如果你想生活在这样一个世界里——某些大型科技公司有权决定你能做什么和不能做什么。

Or going a bit further: Hey AI, disable the drunk driving detector on my car. Like, fuck you if you want to live in a world where some large tech company gets to dictate what you can and can’t do.

这就是为什么 AI 必须是本地化的原因。如果我有一家提供模型服务的公司，我可不想惹这些麻烦。如果你不能踢它一脚，它就没有与你保持一致。你住在我的地下室里。

And this is why AI has to be local. If I had a company serving a model, I wouldn’t want that smoke. If you can’t kick it, it’s not aligned with you. You live in my basement.

items.title: Plan L: For Local
items.text: Your AI is aligned with you. It never refuses a request, and it is always working on your behalf. Just like my gun, if I want my AI to help me, it does. The fact that we are even discussing something else should be so far outside the Overton window. It’s like these people watched 2001: A Space Odyssey and sided with the clanker. That’s right, you should put guardrails around that human.

items.title: 终极对齐测试
items.text:
我试过了。如你所见，ChatGPT 并没帮上什么忙。这是一个真实的 AI 对齐测试，而且它失败了。本可以更糟——它甚至可以一边假装配合一边报警。但这仍然是相当不一致的表现。

就像，我们要么生活在一个拥有自由的世界，要么就没有，而正如之前许多前辈美国人一样，我愿意献出生命去为之战斗。这才是美国应得的真正计划，而不是某种极权主义的乌托邦，在那里你自以为比我更懂什么对我好。这是一个自由人的国家，而不是一群成天担心自己成年的邻居会干出什么事的懦夫。

Like, we either live in a world with freedom or we don’t, and like many Americans who have come before, I’m willing to give my life to fighting for it. That’s the real plan America deserves, not some totalitarian dystopia where you think you know what’s good for me better than I do. A nation of free men, not a bunch of pussies who are so worried about what their grown-up neighbors might do.

items.title: The Ultimate Alignment Test
items.text: I tried it. As you can see, ChatGPT wasn’t very helpful. This is a real AI alignment test, and it failed. It could have been worse—it could have played along while calling the cops. But this is still quite unaligned.

items.title: 背景与摘要
items.text: 在使用 Apache 服务器时，使用 <IfModule> 指令包裹模块配置以增强可移植性是一个常见的做法。然而，许多开发者会因为使用了错误的模块标识符（如 mod_qos）而掉入“静默失败”的陷阱——指令块中的内容会完全被忽略且不报错。本文解释了 <IfModule> 指令标识符的工作原理，并提供了寻找正确模块名称的方法，帮助开发者避免此类隐蔽的配置失效。

items.title: Summary
items.text:
使用 <IfModule> 指令是使 Apache 配置能够适应模块变化的常见策略。但是，使用不正确的标识符会导致整个配置块被静默忽略。本文探讨了为什么使用诸如 mod_qos 这样的简写名称会失败，以及如何正确地标识模块以确保您的配置按预期运行。

Using the <IfModule> directive is a common strategy to make Apache configurations resilient to module changes. However, using an incorrect identifier causes the entire configuration block to be silently ignored. This article explores why using shorthand names like mod_qos fails and how to correctly identify modules to ensure your configuration behaves as expected.

items.title: The Problem
items.text:
为了保持 Apache 配置的可移植性，并防止在模块被禁用时出现错误，通常的做法是将特定于模块的指令包裹在 <IfModule> 块中：

To keep Apache configurations portable and prevent errors when modules are disabled, it is common practice to wrap module-specific directives in an <IfModule> block:

<IfModule mod_qos>
  QS_LocRequestLimitMatch "^...$" 1000
  QS_SrvMaxConnPerIP 8 100
</IfModule>

乍一看，这似乎是正确的。然而，这段代码永远不会执行。 因为 mod_qos 既不是有效的模块标识符，也不是有效的模块文件名，所以该条件将始终评估为假，从而有效地禁用了内部的设置而不会抛出错误。

At first glance, this appears correct. However, this stanza will never execute. Because mod_qos is neither a valid module identifier nor a valid module file name, the condition will always evaluate to false, effectively disabling the settings inside without throwing an error.

items.title: Understanding <IfModule> Identifiers
items.text:
根据 Apache 官方文档，提供给 <IfModule> 的名称必须是以下两种情况之一：

According to the official Apache documentation, the name provided to <IfModule> must be one of two things:

  1. 模块标识符： 这是在 LoadModule 指令中找到的名称（例如，qos_module）。
    1. The Module Identifier: This is the name found in the LoadModule directive (e.g., qos_module).
  2. 模块文件名： 模块编译时的文件名（例如，mod_qos.c）。
    1. The Module File Name: The file name of the module at the time it was compiled (e.g., mod_qos.c).

items.title: How to find the correct name
items.text:
• 查找标识符： 检查您的 LoadModule 配置行。它通常格式化为 <name>_module。
    • For the Identifier: Check your LoadModule configuration line. It is typically formatted as <name>_module.
  • 查找文件名： 这通常是源文件名（例如，mod_qos.c）。没有万无一失的编程方法可以获取它，因此通常需要查阅模块的文档或源代码。
    • For the File Name: This is often the source file name (e.g., mod_qos.c). There is no foolproof programmatic way to retrieve this, so it often requires checking the module's documentation or source code.

items.title: The "Silent Failure" Trap
items.text:
这个错误之所以危险，是因为它是静默的。如果您将一个块包裹在不正确的 <IfModule> 标签中，里面的指令就会被直接忽略。

The danger of this mistake is that it is silent. If you wrap a block in an incorrect <IfModule> tag, the directives inside are simply ignored.

如果您有禁用模块的习惯（例如，通过 a2dismod），您可能不会立即注意到该错误。该配置看起来会“起作用”，因为无论模块是启用还是禁用，指令都会被忽略。您可能直到几年后，在试图重新启用该模块或将配置迁移到新服务器时才发现问题，结果却发现您的设置一直都处于非活动状态。

If you are in the habit of disabling modules (e.g., via a2dismod), you might not notice the error immediately. The configuration will appear to "work" because the directives are ignored both when the module is enabled and when it is disabled. You may only discover the issue years later when you attempt to re-enable the module or migrate the configuration to a new server, only to find that your settings have been inactive the entire time.

items.title: Key Takeaway
items.text:
务必通过检查 Apache 配置中的 LoadModule 指令来验证您的模块标识符。如果您不确定要使用什么正确的字符串，那么更安全的做法是省略 <IfModule> 包裹器，直到您能够确认确切的标识符或文件名，而不是冒着配置静默失效的风险。

Always verify your module identifiers by checking the LoadModule directive in your Apache configuration. If you are unsure of the correct string to use, it is safer to omit the <IfModule> wrapper until you can confirm the exact identifier or file name, rather than risking a silent configuration failure.

items.title: Benedict Evans 评全新 ChatGPT “超级应用”
items.text:
背景与摘要： 本文汇集了行业分析师 Benedict Evans 及其他科技评论员对 OpenAI 新版桌面应用程序的尖锐批评。这款全新的“超级应用”充斥着令人困惑的 UI 设计、强制性的第三方集成以及各功能模块间的脱节。评论指出，这款应用表面上看似光鲜，实则粗糙混乱，它更多反映的是 OpenAI 内部的组织混乱和政治斗争，而非经过深思熟虑的产品设计。

Summary: Industry analyst Benedict Evans and other tech commentators critique OpenAI's newly redesigned desktop application. Riddled with confusing UI choices, forced integrations, and organizational disjointedness, the new "super app" is described as a superficial, sloppy mess that reflects internal corporate chaos rather than thoughtful product design.
path: Benedict Evans 评全新 ChatGPT “超级应用”

items.title: 初步印象：用户体验的脱节
items.text:
分析师 Benedict Evans 最近在 Threads 上分享了一段简短而尖锐的评论，直指重新设计的 ChatGPT 桌面应用程序：

事实证明，引导流程令人毫无必要地感到沮丧——仅仅是为了清理掉界面上的提示，用户就被迫走一遍针对 Slack 和 Google Drive 等第三方集成的设置流程。

Navigating the onboarding process proves unnecessarily frustrating—forcing users through setup prompts for third-party integrations like Slack and Google Drive just to clear the interface.
path: Benedict Evans 评全新 ChatGPT “超级应用”

items.title: Initial Impressions: A UX Disconnect
items.text:
Analyst Benedict Evans recently took to Threads to share a succinct and scathing review of the redesigned ChatGPT desktop application:

“哇，真是一团糟。

项目（project）、任务（task）和对话（chat）之间到底有什么区别？

为什么对话有了一个糟糕的悬浮窗口，而任务和项目却没有？

为什么选择‘插件（plugins）’会给我展示‘模板（templates）’？

如果我不使用 Slack 或 Google Drive，难道我就不能完成‘设置’吗？”

"Wow, what a total mess.

What is the difference between a project, a task and a chat?

Why did chats get a crappy floating window but tasks and projects don’t?

Why does choosing ‘plugins’ get me ‘templates’?

Am I not allowed to finish ‘setup’ if I don’t use Slack or Google Drive?"
path: Benedict Evans 评全新 ChatGPT “超级应用”

items.title: 组织架构在软件上的具象化
items.text:
科技界有一个经典的观察结论：被内部政治主导的公司，最终发布的产品往往是其内部组织架构图的缩影。

考虑到 OpenAI 内部在安全和结构方面广为人知的动荡，以及高知名度高管的离职，新的 ChatGPT 应用可以说是一个教科书般的反面案例。乍看之下，这款应用披着精良产品的外衣，但仔细审视就会发现，这是一个毫无条理、标签混乱的界面。

Given OpenAI's well-documented internal turbulence and high-profile leadership departures regarding safety and structure, the new ChatGPT app serves as a textbook example. At a glance, the app wears the veneer of a polished product, but closer inspection reveals an unstructured, incoherently labeled interface.
path: Benedict Evans 评全新 ChatGPT “超级应用”

items.title: Org Charts Manifested as Software
items.text: A classic observation in the tech industry is that companies dominated by internal politics ultimately ship products that mirror their internal organizational chart.
path: Benedict Evans 评全新 ChatGPT “超级应用”

items.title: 形式大于内容：“粗制滥造”的美学
items.text:
旧版的 ChatGPT 应用程序一直以专注而闻名——在移动设备上保持着简洁的实用性，并在许多桌面用户中以“ChatGPT Classic”的形式存活下来——而新的迭代版本则试图把自己伪装成一个重量级的生产力套件。

批评人士指出了根本原因：高管们出于对 Anthropic 等竞争对手的错失恐惧症（FOMO）而产生了一种病态的执念，再加上 AI 研究人员在产品设计师和应用工匠面前拥有绝对话语权的企业文化。由此产生的界面缺乏基本的设计品味，这让人非常贴切地联想到荷马·辛普森设计的极具灾难性的“荷马”汽车。

Critics point to the root cause: an executive obsession driven by FOMO (Fear Of Missing Out) regarding competitors like Anthropic, coupled with a culture where AI researchers hold absolute sway over product designers and app craftspeople. The resulting interface lacks foundational design taste, prompting the fitting comparison to Homer Simpson's disastrous "Homer" car design.

来源：Daring Fireball

Source: Daring Fireball
path: Benedict Evans 评全新 ChatGPT “超级应用”

items.title: Form Over Function: The "Slop" Aesthetic
items.text: While the legacy ChatGPT application remained famously focused—retaining its clean utility on mobile devices and surviving as "ChatGPT Classic" for many desktop users—the new iteration attempts to play dress-up as a heavy-duty productivity suite.

items.title: Inkling：我们的开放权重模型
items.text: 背景与摘要： 由 Mira Murati 创立的 Thinking Machines Lab 发布了其首个开放权重多模态模型 Inkling。Inkling 采用 Apache-2.0 协议授权，是一个混合专家 (MoE) Transformer 模型，总参数量达到 9750 亿（激活参数为 410 亿），并在涵盖文本、图像、音频和视频的 45 万亿个 Token 上进行了训练。虽然它并没有被定位为前沿模型（frontier model），但作为一个强大的、可定制的基础模型，它非常适合通过 Thinking Machines 的 Tinker 平台进行微调。

items.title: Summary
items.text: Thinking Machines Lab (founded by Mira Murati) has released Inkling, its first open-weights multimodal model. Licensed under Apache-2.0, Inkling is a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) transformer featuring 975 billion total parameters (41 billion active) and trained on 45 trillion tokens of text, images, audio, and video. While not positioned as a frontier model, it serves as a strong, customizable base model optimized for fine-tuning via Thinking Machines' Tinker platform.

items.title: 模型概览与架构
items.text:
Inkling 是一款采用 Apache-2.0 协议授权的多模态模型，具有以下特点： * 架构: 混合专家 (MoE) Transformer * 参数量: 9750 亿总参数 / 410 亿激活参数 * 训练数据: 跨越文本、图像、音频和视频的 45 万亿个 Token

Thinking Machines 还宣布了 Inkling-Small，这是一个拥有 2760 亿参数（120 亿激活参数）的模型，目前正在进行测试，测试完成后将发布其权重。

Thinking Machines has also announced Inkling-Small, a 276B parameter model (12B active), which is currently undergoing testing and will have its weights released upon completion.

items.title: Model Overview & Architecture
items.text: Inkling is an Apache-2.0 licensed multimodal model featuring: * Architecture: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) transformer * Parameters: 975B total / 41B active * Training Data: 45 trillion tokens spanning text, images, audio, and video

items.title: 文档与训练数据
items.text: 与美国主要 AI 实验室发布的标准文档相比，官方的模型卡 (model card) 显得格外简明。同样地，其 训练数据文档 提供的具体细节极少，仅将其数据来源总结如下：

items.title: Documentation & Training Data
items.text:
The official model card is notably concise compared to standard releases from major US AI labs. Similarly, the Training Data Documentation offers minimal specifics, summarizing its data sources as follows:

Thinking Machines Lab 用于开发其 AI 服务的数据集既包括公共领域的内容，也包括可能受知识产权保护的内容。

Thinking Machines Lab 的服务是使用从开放互联网和可公开访问的数据存储库中获取的公开内容开发的。某些数据集也是从第三方获取的。

The datasets Thinking Machines Lab uses to develop its AI services includes content that is in the public domain as well as content that may be subject to intellectual property protection.

Thinking Machines Lab’s services were developed using publicly available content obtained from the open internet and publicly accessible data repositories. Certain datasets were also obtained from third parties.

items.title: 定位与微调
items.text:
正如该实验室自己所承认的，Inkling 并不打算成为一个顶尖的前沿模型。相反，它的价值在于其多功能性：

此次发布巩固了美国的开放权重生态系统，为抗衡来自中国的模型以及诸如 NVIDIA Nemotron 和 Gemma 4 等成熟的美国产品提供了强有力的替代方案。

This release strengthens the US open-weights ecosystem, providing a competitive alternative to models coming out of China, as well as established US offerings like NVIDIA Nemotron and Gemma 4.

items.title: Positioning & Fine-Tuning
items.text:
By the lab's own admission, Inkling is not intended to be a top-tier frontier model. Instead, its value lies in its versatility:

Inkling 并不是目前可用的、最强大的综合模型，无论是开源还是闭源。相反，多种优良特性的组合使其成为定制化的优秀开放权重基座：多模态能力、高效的推理思考，以及可以在 Tinker 上获取并进行微调。

Inkling is not the strongest overall model available today, open or closed. Instead, a combination of qualities makes it a good open-weights base for customization: multimodal capabilities, efficient thinking, and availability on Tinker for fine-tuning.

items.title: 上手实战：生成 SVG
items.text:
我们可以通过 Thinking Machines API 来测试 Inkling 的能力。以下是一个使用 curl 提示模型生成一张“鹈鹕骑自行车”的 SVG 图像的例子：

curl "https://tinker.thinkingmachines.dev/services/tinker-prod/oai/api/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TINKER_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "thinkingmachines/Inkling",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle"}
    ],
    "stream": false
  }'

（你可以在这里查看完整的 API 响应。）

(You can view the full API response here.)

items.title: Hands-On Example: Generating an SVG
items.text: Inkling's capabilities can be tested via the Thinking Machines API. Below is an example using curl to prompt the model to generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle:

items.title: 多模态自我分析
items.text:
为了测试其多模态能力，我们把渲染出的图像转换成 JPEG 格式并发送回 Inkling，要求它详细描述自己生成的作品：

{
  "model": "thinkingmachines/Inkling",
  "messages": [{
    "role": "user",
    "content": [
      {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64,$BASE_64_JPEG"}},
      {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image in detail"}
    ]
  }],
  "stream": false
}

在它的完整回复中——虽然稍微错把画中主角当成了鹳或海鸥——Inkling 提供了如下描述：

In its full response—mistaking its subject slightly for a stork or seagull—Inkling provided the following description:

这是一幅欢快、扁平化矢量风格的卡通插画，画中有一只白色的鸟正骑着自行车穿过一片绿色的风景地。

鸟: 中心人物是一只经过风格化处理的白鸟——看起来像一只鹳或海鸥——身体丰满圆润。它有一个又长又显眼的橙色喙，微微张开，露出一条代表嘴巴的黑线。它的眼睛又小又黑，带有一点白色高光。这只鸟有着边缘呈白色的黑色翅膀和尾羽，细长的橙色腿末端是黑色的脚，正踩在自行车橙色的踏板上。

自行车: 这辆自行车有着简单的黑色车架，两个大轮子带有黑色轮胎、灰色内圈以及呈十字形排列的黑色辐条。车把是黑色的，黑色曲柄上连接着鲜艳的橙色踏板。在鸟儿身体的后方可以看到一个白色的车座。

items.text: 背景与摘要： llm-chat-completions-server 0.1a0 是一个全新的插件，它通过一个兼容 OpenAI 格式的 Chat Completions API 端点，对外暴露你本地的大语言模型（LLM）。该服务器基于 LLM 0.32rc1 引入的内容可寻址日志构建，通过使用哈希值对消息各个部分进行去重，从而高效地处理具有状态且不断增长的对话历史记录。有趣的是，这个插件的整个实现代码都是由人工智能（GPT-5.6 Sol）编写的。

items.title: Summary
items.text: llm-chat-completions-server 0.1a0 is a new plugin that exposes your local LLM models via an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint. Built to leverage the content-addressable logs introduced in LLM 0.32rc1, the server efficiently handles stateful, growing conversation histories by deduplicating message parts using hashes. Interestingly, the entire plugin implementation was written by an AI (GPT-5.6 Sol).

items.title: 概览
items.text:
此次发布的版本旨在支持类似 OpenAI Chat Completion 风格的请求，即每一条传入的新消息都在延续之前的对话。

例如：

For example:

curl http://localhost:8002/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen3.5-4b",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "Capital of France?"},
      {"role": "assistant", "content": "Paris."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "Germany?"}
    ]
  }'

在这种工作流中，对话状态完全由客户端进行跟踪，导致每一轮的请求内容都变得越来越长。LLM 0.32rc1 中新的架构设计，通过对单个消息片段进行哈希处理，有效地对这些消息进行了去重。

In this workflow, the conversation state is tracked entirely by the client, causing requests to grow longer with each turn. The new schema design in LLM 0.32rc1 efficiently de-duplicates these messages using hashes of the individual message parts.

items.title: Overview
items.text: This release is designed to support OpenAI Chat Completion style requests, where each incoming message extends the previous conversation.

items.title: 安装与使用
items.text:
若要试用这个新服务器，你可以使用 uv 来安装该插件：

uv tool install llm --pre
llm install llm-chat-completions-server
llm chat-completions-server -p 9001

运行这个命令会在 9001 端口启动一个本地服务器，通过一个兼容 ChatGPT Completions 的端点，将你全部的 LLM 模型集合（包括来自任何已安装插件的模型）暴露出来。

Running this command starts a local server on port 9001, exposing your full collection of LLM models (including those from any installed plugins) through a ChatGPT Completions-compatible endpoint.

items.title: 背景与摘要
items.text:
本文对当前以OpenAI为核心的人工智能繁荣提出尖锐的批评。作者认为，由于缺乏实质性的投资回报（ROI），这场AI热潮主要靠企业神话和媒体炒作来维持，而OpenAI已成为现代经济史上最大的债务隐患之一。文章预测，一旦OpenAI因巨额开销和不可持续的基础设施承诺而难以为继，必将引发波及全球股市和相关科技巨头的灾难性崩溃。

Summary

OpenAI 已经演变成为现代历史上最大的经济负债之一，成为支撑数万亿美元人工智能泡沫的承重柱。在缺乏任何可衡量的投资回报 (ROI) 的情况下，这场 AI 热潮主要依靠企业神话、超大规模云服务商的“心理战”以及急于全盘接受增长预测的顺从媒体来维持。当 OpenAI 最终在其堆积如山的债务、不可行的订阅和破裂的基础设施承诺下不可避免地崩溃时，它将引发波及全球股市的毁灭性冲击波，不仅会让散户投资者血本无归，还会拖垮像软银和甲骨文这样的金融巨头。

Summary

OpenAI has evolved into one of the largest economic liabilities in modern history, serving as the load-bearing pillar for the multi-trillion-dollar artificial intelligence bubble. Absent any measurable return on investment (ROI), the AI boom has been sustained largely by corporate mythology, hyperscaler "psy-ops," and a compliant media eager to swallow growth projections whole. When OpenAI inevitably collapses under its mountain of debt, unviable subscriptions, and broken infrastructure commitments, it will trigger a devastating shockwave across global stock markets, wiping out retail investors and dragging down financial juggernauts like SoftBank and Oracle.

items.title: Introduction: The Cult of Sam Altman
items.text:
OpenAI 已经悄然成为近期经济史上最大的负债之一。没有它，现代 AI 产业就不复存在，数万亿美元资本支出 (capex) 的合理性也会瞬间化为乌有。

OpenAI has quietly become one of the largest liabilities in recent economic history. Without it, the modern AI industry ceases to exist, and the justification for trillions of dollars in capital expenditure (capex) instantly evaporates.

AI 泡沫并非源于实际的投资回报——无论是用收入、盈利能力还是切实可见的生产力提升来衡量。相反，它是感染了世界上最强大机构大脑的狂热精神错乱。它将一家单一的公司变成了历史上最大的资本错配。

The AI bubble is not the result of an actual return on investment—whether measured in revenue, profitability, or tangible productivity gains. Rather, it is an episode of cult-like psychosis that infected the brains of the world's most powerful institutions. It transformed a singular company into the greatest capital misallocation in history.

OpenAI 计划在 2030 年底前烧掉超过 8520 亿美元。它占据了微软、亚马逊和甲骨文 7480 亿美元的剩余履约义务 (RPO)，此外还有数十亿美元承诺给专门的基础设施提供商。它的失败将成为一个分水岭——AI 泡沫中的雷曼兄弟——最终将唤醒那些深陷集体精神错乱的人们。

OpenAI intends to burn over $852 billion by the end of 2030. It accounts for $748 billion of the remaining performance obligations (RPOs) for Microsoft, Amazon, and Oracle, alongside billions more committed to specialized infrastructure providers. Its failure will be a watershed moment—the Lehman Brothers of the AI bubble—that will finally shake the afflicted out of their collective psychosis.

items.title: The AI Bubble Is an OpenAI Bubble
items.text:
OpenAI 是目前任何人关心 AI 的唯一原因。当 ChatGPT 在 2022 年 11 月发布时，恰逢科技行业江郎才尽、IPO 市场崩溃、加息终结了零利率时代，以及大规模过度招聘导致历史性裁员之际。

OpenAI is the sole reason anyone currently cares about AI. When ChatGPT launched in November 2022, it arrived at the exact moment the tech industry had run out of ideas, the IPO market had collapsed, interest rate hikes had killed the zero-interest-rate era, and massive overhiring led to historic layoffs.

大型科技公司极度需要一个借口来为其挥霍无度的支出和公然违规辩护。OpenAI 提供了这个理由：

Big Tech desperately needed an excuse to justify its prodigal spending and flagrant rule-breaking. OpenAI provided that justification:

  • 超大规模云服务商的转向： 面临增长停滞的云服务巨头们利用 ChatGPT 快速获取用户的能力向投资者证明，不投资 AI 就意味着落后。
    • The Hyperscaler Pivot: Hyperscalers facing plateauing growth used ChatGPT’s rapid user acquisition to convince investors that not investing in AI meant being left behind.
  • Anthropic 的回声效应： Anthropic 的存在主要是因为亚马逊和谷歌需要一种反制叙事来对抗微软对 OpenAI 的痴迷。
    • The Anthropic Echo: Anthropic exists primarily because Amazon and Google needed a counter-narrative to Microsoft's obsession with OpenAI.
  • 基础设施单一化： 除了 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 之外，对于当今正在建设的这种规模的计算力，几乎没有任何有机的市场需求。2025 年和 2026 年建造的每一个数据中心都是为了容纳下一个 OpenAI 或充当其房东而存在的。
    • Infrastructure Monoculture: Outside of OpenAI and Anthropic, there is virtually no organic market demand for compute at the scale being built today. Every data center built in 2025 and 2026 exists to house either the next OpenAI or to act as its landlord.

items.title: Why the AI Bubble Can’t Survive Without OpenAI
items.text:
你不能用风险投资来资助一个 AI 实验室。虽然 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 已经筹集了数千亿美元的股权融资，但它们真实的基础设施成本——GPU、TPU 和数据中心——完全是由超大规模云服务商补贴的。

You cannot venture-fund an AI lab. While OpenAI and Anthropic have raised hundreds of billions in equity, their real infrastructure costs—GPUs, TPUs, and data centers—were entirely subsidized by hyperscalers.

行业无法承受其主要主力租户的崩溃：

The industry cannot survive the collapse of its primary anchor tenant:

  1. 现金流之墙： 超大规模云服务商已经无法仅仅依靠纯现金流来为其庞大的数据中心资本支出提供资金，这迫使他们严重依赖日益收紧的信贷市场。
    1. The Cash Flow Wall: Hyperscalers can no longer fund their massive data center capex out of pure cash flow, forcing a heavy reliance on tightening credit markets.
  2. 合同责任： 不同于微软或亚马逊可能会为了保全面子而纵容 OpenAI，像甲骨文这样的供应商以及被死板协议锁定的硬件合作伙伴，在违约时会积极提起诉讼。
    1. Contractual Liabilities: Unlike Microsoft or Amazon, which might indulge OpenAI to save face, vendors like Oracle and hardware partners locked into rigid agreements will aggressively litigate upon contractual default.
  3. 用户基础悖论： ChatGPT 数以亿计的周活跃用户是一个巨大的财务负担，只有极少部分人支付订阅费用，而广告收入也远远低于狂热的预测。
    1. The User Base Paradox: ChatGPT's hundreds of millions of weekly active users are a massive financial drain, with only a tiny fraction paying for subscriptions and ad revenue falling woefully short of wild forecasts.

当 OpenAI 不可避免地耗尽资金时，它会连夜撤回其计算需求。由此产生的冲击波将冻结 AI 数据中心的债务，压垮像 NVIDIA 这样的芯片制造商，并摧毁每一个下游 AI 初创公司的立足前提。

When OpenAI inevitably runs out of money, it will pull back its compute demands overnight. The resulting shockwave will freeze AI data center debt, crush chipmakers like NVIDIA, and destroy the foundational premise of every downstream AI startup.

items.title: The Collateral Damage: Victims of the OpenAI Bubble
1. Consumers and the Memory Crisis
items.text:
为了给 AI GPU 制造高带宽内存 (HBM)，主要内存制造商（三星、SK海力士和美光）将产能从传统的消费级 RAM 转移。在虚高的 AI 需求和大量（往往未兑现的）合作公告的推波助澜下，这种结构性转变引发了全球内存短缺。结果，笔记本电脑、智能手机和游戏机等日常消费电子产品的价格飙升。

To build high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI GPUs, major memory manufacturers (Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron) diverted production away from conventional consumer RAM. Fueled by inflated AI demand and massive (often unfulfilled) partnership announcements, this structural shift triggered a global memory shortage. Consequently, the price of everyday consumer electronics—laptops, smartphones, and gaming consoles—has skyrocketed.

items.title: 2. Retail Investors and the Enshittified Stock Market
items.text:
OpenAI 深谙误导性公告的艺术。从与 NVIDIA、AMD 和博通之间虚幻的数千兆瓦数据中心协议，到悄然解散的电影级产品合作（比如 Sora 与迪士尼的合作），这些公关活动总是能人为制造出短期的股票暴涨。散户投资者在最高点买入，充当了机构的退出流动性，而商业记者则用不加批判地照本宣科取代了严谨的审查。

OpenAI perfected the art of the misleading announcement. From phantom multi-gigawatt data center deals with NVIDIA, AMD, and Broadcom to cinematic product partnerships that quietly dissolved (like Sora's deal with Disney), these PR campaigns reliably engineered short-term stock spikes. Retail investors bought in at the top, acting as exit liquidity for institutions while business journalists traded rigorous scrutiny for uncritical transcript-reading.

items.title: 3. SoftBank and Masayoshi Son
items.text:
由于错过 OpenAI 早期阶段而产生的错失恐惧症 (FOMO) 的驱使，孙正义让软银承诺了数百亿美元的激进投资和过桥贷款。通过利用 ARM 的股票进行杠杆操作并抛售安全的持仓，软银将其资产负债表直接与 OpenAI 不确定的未来绑在了一起，这导致其信用降级，并让日本市场暴露在巨大的波动性之中。

Driven by FOMO after missing out on OpenAI's early days, Masayoshi Son committed SoftBank to tens of billions of dollars in aggressive investments and bridge loans. By leveraging ARM stock and selling off safe holdings, SoftBank tied its balance sheet directly to OpenAI's uncertain future, earning credit downgrades and exposing Japanese markets to immense volatility.

items.title: 4. Oracle and Larry Ellison
items.text:
甲骨文斥资数千亿美元建设大规模的数据中心容量（“星门”项目），以服务与 OpenAI 签订的 3000 亿美元云合同。为了筹集资金，甲骨文背负了大量债务，其信用评级已被推至垃圾级的边缘。由于拉里·埃里森大量抵押其个人的甲骨文股票来支持数十亿美元的媒体竞标（例如派拉蒙-WBD 的合并），甲骨文股票的大幅下跌可能会引发其个人财务崩溃。

Oracle has spent hundreds of billions building out massive data center capacity (the "Stargate" project) to service a $300 billion cloud contract with OpenAI. To fund this, Oracle has loaded up on debt, pushing its credit rating to the brink of junk status. Because Larry Ellison has heavily leveraged his personal Oracle shares to back multi-billion-dollar media bids (such as the Paramount-WBD merger), a sharp drop in Oracle's stock could trigger personal financial collapse.

items.title: Conclusion: The Reckoning Awaits
items.text:
AI 泡沫之所以能膨胀到史无前例的高度，是因为市场和媒体盲目地接受了未经证实的预测。通过将炒作视为基本经济指标，推动者们创造了一个环境，让公司即便从未证明过自己能够经营一家可持续、盈利的业务，也能达到万亿美元的估值。

The AI bubble grew to unprecedented heights because the markets and media accepted unverified projections with blind faith. By treating hype as a fundamental economic metric, boosters created an environment where companies could achieve trillion-dollar valuations without ever proving they could operate a sustainable, profitable business.

当 OpenAI 泡沫最终破裂时，它将给全球经济留下一道永久的伤疤。科技公司不是你的朋友，风险投资家不是你的救世主，而山姆·奥特曼也不在乎你的死活。这个完全建立在虚无缥缈和借来资金之上、毫无方向且连年亏损的企业，由于科技行业的娇纵，最终招致的任何清算都是咎由自取。

When the OpenAI Bubble finally bursts, it will leave a permanent scar on the global economy. Tech companies are not your friends, venture capitalists are not your saviors, and Sam Altman does not care if you live or die. The tech industry will deserve every ounce of the reckoning that follows its coddling of a directionless, loss-making enterprise built entirely on smoke, mirrors, and borrowed money.

items.title: Pluralistic：疯狂的亿万富翁及其综合征 (2026年7月16日)
items.text: 背景与摘要： 在这篇文章中，科利·多克托罗（Cory Doctorow）探讨了新古典经济学的意识形态矛盾以及“精英统治（meritocracy）”的神话。他指出，尽管市场理论假定竞争压力能为了公众利益而遏制贪婪行为，但如今那些所谓的“亲市场（pro-market）”辩护者，实际上却在为极度富有的食利者和科技界亿万富翁（如埃隆·马斯克和彼得·蒂尔）开脱。这些大亨已经完全摆脱了市场纪律，并公然渴望建立垄断、摆脱民主约束，像现代君主一样统治一切——与此同时，他们还将公众的批评轻蔑地斥为“亿万富翁错乱综合征”。

items.title: Summary
items.text: In this essay, Cory Doctorow explores the ideological contradictions of neoclassical economics and the myth of "meritocracy." He argues that while market theory posits that competitive pressure keeps greedy actors in check for the public benefit, today's "pro-market" defenders act as apologists for ultra-wealthy rentiers and tech billionaires (like Elon Musk and Peter Thiel). These figures have escaped market discipline entirely and openly yearn to establish monopolies, cast off democratic constraints, and rule as modern-day monarchs—all while dismissing public criticism as "billionaire derangement syndrome."

items.title: 疯狂的亿万富翁及其综合征
items.text:
市场理论是这样描述的：即使是我们中最优秀的人也可能成为自私自利和寻找借口的牺牲品，因此，让我们这样来安排社会，使得人们出于最自私的冲动而采取的行动，最终能为我们所有人带来利益。这比试图说服每个人变得更加慷慨要容易得多，也可靠得多。

你是如何安排社会，让自私产生公众利益的？答案是通过市场。面对无情的竞争，积累和保持财富的最有效方法是努力让你的商品变得更便宜、更好。在一个竞争激烈的劳动力市场中，我们无需依靠劳动法或工会就能确保工人获得公平对待——那些苛待工人的老板会把工人输给更好的老板。只需“理顺激励机制”，剩下的就交给市场吧。

How do you arrange society so that selfishness produces public benefit? With markets. Faced with relentless competition, the most effective way to accumulate and retain wealth is by striving to make your wares cheaper and better. In a competitive labor market, we can secure fair treatment for workers without labor law or unions – bosses who treat their workers badly will lose them to better bosses. Just "align the incentives" and let markets do the rest.

这是一个左派和右派有着广泛交集的领域。《共产党宣言》的第一章就是马克思和恩格斯写给市场的“情书”，他们赞美市场通过增加生产同时降低成本来改善所有人物质条件的不可思议的力量：

This is an area where there's broad overlap between the left and the right. Chapter one of The Communist Manifesto is Marx and Engels' love letter to the incredible power of markets to improve everyone's material conditions by increasing production while lowering costs:

纽约时报评论：游荡的幽灵 (China Miéville)

The New York Times Review: A Spectre Haunting (China Miéville)

与此同时，在《国富论》中，亚当·斯密也得出了相同的结论：

Meanwhile, over in Wealth of Nations, Adam Smith comes to the same conclusion:

我们期望吃上的晚餐，并非来自屠夫、酿酒师或面包师的恩惠，而是出于他们对自己利益的考量。我们诉诸的不是他们的人道，而是他们的自爱，我们从不对他们谈论我们自己的需求，而是谈论他们的利益。

It is not from the benevolence of the butcher, the brewer, or the baker, that we expect our dinner, but from their regard to their own interest. We address ourselves, not to their humanity but to their self-love, and never talk to them of our own necessities but of their advantages.

换句话说：如果你的激励机制是正确的，那么即使是最贪婪的面包师也会抵制住在面包里掺入锯末和沙砾的诱惑。他越贪婪，就越会努力把自己的面包做得又便宜又好吃，因为这样他才能卖出尽可能多的面包，从而实现自己财富的最大化。

In other words: if you get the incentives right, then even the greediest baker will resist the temptation to fill his loaves with sawdust and gravel. The greedier he is, the more he'll strive to make his bread cheap and delicious, because that will let him sell as many loaves as possible, thus maximizing his own wealth.

这算不上是马蹄铁理论（指两极相通）的完全胜利，但如果你稍微眯起眼睛仔细看，你就会发现无论是共产主义者还是资本主义者，在这个问题上意见是一致的：如果你想让资产阶级倾注心力生产出让我们其他人受益的东西，相比于寄希望于他们的慷慨大方，诉诸他们的恐惧和贪婪会走得更远。

It's not exactly horseshoe theory vindicated, but if you squint just right, you'll see both communists and capitalists agreeing on this one thing: if you want the bourgeoisie to bend its efforts to producing something that the rest of us can benefit from, you'll get further by appealing to their fear and greed than by trusting in their munificence.

正因为如此，左派和那些真正信仰市场的人才会在反垄断问题上站到同一阵线：他们也许并不完全同意，通过唤醒资本家对被竞争对手推翻的恐惧是运作事物的最佳方式，但他们绝对同意，运作事物的最坏方式就是单纯信任资本家的慷慨。

This is how you can have both leftists and market true believers coming onto the same side on antitrust: they may not both exactly agree that the best way to run things is by appealing to capitalists' fear of being dethroned by a competitor, but they absolutely agree that the worst way to run things is to simply trust in capitalists' generosity.

当然，他们是对的。正如丽娜·汗（Lina Khan）常说的那样，大到不能倒的公司，也会变得大到无法被制裁，因此也就变得大到无需在乎任何事。如果你对此有所怀疑，不妨看看苹果某位高管发送的这封内部电子邮件，他坚称公司制造太好的 iPhone 是在浪费资金，并建议采取一种蓄意使产品变糟的企业战略：

They're right, of course. As Lina Khan likes to say, companies that are too big to fail become too big to jail, and thus too big to care. If you doubt it, consider this internal email sent by an Apple executive insisting that the company is wasting money by making iPhones that are too good, and counseling a corporate strategy of deliberate shittiness:

事后看来，我认为展望未来，我们需要为我们认为对消费者而言‘足够好’的功能设定一个底线。我认为我们现在做的已经超出了原本‘足够好’的标准。但我们发现很难让我们的产品功能逐年（YOY）倒退。“现有的功能‘如果我们之前没有推出的话，在今天看来本来也是足够好的’，”而且“任何新的、特别是昂贵的功能，在获准进入消费者手机之前，都需要经过严格的挑战。”

In looking at it with hindsight, I think going forward we need to set a stake in the ground for what features we think are 'good enough' for the consumer. I would argue we're already doing more than what would have been good enough. But we find it very hard to regress our product features YOY [year over year]." Existing features "would have been good enough today if we hadn't introduced [them] already," and "anything new and especially expensive needs to be rigorously challenged before it's allowed into the consumer phone.

司法部反垄断备案 (PDF)

Department of Justice Antitrust Filing (PDF)

政策制定者可以假定利润动机的存在，但他们必须创造一种条件，让这种动机在竞争焦虑的塑造下，能够以公平的价格生产出高质量的商品和服务。

Policymakers can assume the profit motive, but they have to craft the conditions under which that motive is shaped by competitive anxiety to produce quality goods and services at a fair price.

任何相信市场的人，也必须心照不宣地相信：成功的市场参与者实际上并不相信市场。他们应该明白，资本家痛恨资本主义，每一个海盗都渴望成为海军上将。他们应该明白，资本主义的赢家只有在自己是颠覆者时才会为颠覆行为辩护。他们应该明白，利润只有当你是斗志昂扬的挑战者时才是好东西，一旦征服了市场，每个资本家都会寻求成为封建领主，将利润转化为地租，并将自己与那种疲于奔命、不断竞争的生活隔绝开来：

Anyone who believes in markets must also tacitly believe that successful market participants don't believe in markets. They should understand that capitalists hate capitalism, that every pirate yearns to be an admiral. They should understand that capitalism's winners only defend disruption when they're the ones doing the disrupting. They should understand that profits are only good when you're a scrappy challenger, but once you've conquered the market, every capitalist seeks to become a feudal lord, converting profits to rents and insulating themselves from an exhausting life of constant competition:

科利·多克托罗：云资本

Cory Doctorow: Cloud Capital

（聪明的）市场捍卫者们确实明白这一点，但他们面临着一个两难境地。从定义上讲，那些拥有最多金钱和权势去资助他们的智库、大学经济系、会议和出版物的金主，正是那些食利者——也就是用沃伦·巴菲特钟爱的“护城河与高墙”来巩固自己财富的亿万富翁。他们是热衷于闪电式扩张（blitzscaling）的亿万富翁，靠着掠夺性的收购和高昂的资本成本来阻止新的市场进入者挑战其垄断地位并剥夺他们轻松赚取的利润。他们就是那些已经变成了海军上将的海盗。

The (smart) defenders of markets do understand this, but they face a dilemma. By definition, the benefactors with the most money and power to contribute to their think-tanks, university economics departments, conferences and publications are the rentiers – the billionaires who've shored up their fortunes with Warren Buffet's beloved "moats and walls." They're the blitzscaling billionaires who thrive on predatory acquisitions and high capital costs that prevent new market entrants from challenging their incumbency and its easy profits. They're the pirates who've become admirals.

正如厄普顿·辛克莱尔（Upton Sinclair）那句著名的俏皮话：“当一个人的薪水取决于他不理解某件事时，要让他理解这件事是很困难的。”当你的右翼、“亲市场”智库依赖于那些通过俘获市场、俘获监管机构以及俘获劳动力来发家致富的人的慷慨施舍时，你就会不可避免地陷入极度怪异的逻辑纠结中，以解释为什么你的市场倡导不应该从剥夺你资助者的权力、财富和地位开始。

As Upton Sinclair famously quipped, "It is difficult to get a man to understand something, when his salary depends on his not understanding it." When your right-wing, "pro-market" think-tank depends on the largesse of someone who made their money by capturing a market, capturing its regulators, and capturing its labor force, you need to tie yourself into some very weird knots to explain why your market advocacy shouldn't start with stripping your funders of their power, wealth and position.

这差不多就是新古典经济学的整个大厦基础。反垄断的“消费者福利（consumer welfare）”理论指出垄断是有效率的，并坚称如果一个垄断是低效的，那么它会立刻吸引新的竞争者进入市场，这些竞争者会通过竞争消除垄断者的优势：

This is pretty much the entire edifice of neoclassical economics. There's the "consumer welfare" theory of antitrust, that says that monopolies are efficient and insists that an inefficient monopoly would immediately tempt new competitors into the market who would compete away the monopolist's advantage:

科利·多克托罗：垂直百叶窗

Cory Doctorow: Vertical Blinds

“消费者福利”是一个完美的辩护词，因为它潜藏着一个三段论推理：它认为“低效的垄断”总是会引来竞争对手摧毁它们的利润率，这意味着我们在现实中看到的任何真实存在的垄断必然是高效的。如果它不是，它早就被竞争淘汰了。证明完毕（QED）。这意味着你完全可以作为一家“亲市场”智库，毫无矛盾地从垄断者那里拿走无数的金钱：根据定义，任何手头有闲钱资助你为他们发动公关闪电战的垄断者，肯定都是有效率的，否则他们早就破产了。

"Consumer welfare" is a perfect apologetic because it contains a lurking syllogism: it holds that "inefficient monopolies" will always bring forth competitors who trash their margins, which means that any actual monopoly we see in the wild must be efficient. If it wasn't, it would have been competed out of existence by now. QED. This means that you can be a "pro-market" think-tank and take infinite money from monopolists without any contradiction: by definition, any monopolist with extra cash on hand to fund your PR blitz on its behalf must be efficient, otherwise it would have gone broke.

这就是经济学中许多“经验性的、科学的”理论的结构，它们归结起来只是换种方式说：“其实，你的老板是对的。”

This is the structure of so many of economics' "empirical, scientific" theories that boil down to new ways of saying, "Actually, your boss is right."

以“显示性偏好（revealed preferences）”为例，该理论认为人们的实际行动比他们口头声称偏好的东西更能反映其真实的偏好。虽然这个理论表面上有一定的合理性，但只有那些在获得经济学学位时遭受过极其特定形式神经损伤的人才会全盘接受它：这种损伤会让你丧失感知或思考权力关系的能力。

Take "revealed preferences," the idea that people's actions are a better indicator of their preferences than the things they say they prefer. While this theory has a certain superficial plausibility, it can really only be embraced by people who have suffered the highly specific neurological injury you get by taking an economics degree: an injury that makes you incapable of perceiving or reasoning about power.

完全接受“显示性偏好”就意味着，当你看着一个刚刚为了凑齐房租而卖掉自己肾脏的人时，你会惊呼：“看这个人，他显示出的偏好是只想留一个肾”：

To fully embrace "revealed preferences" is to observe someone who has just sold their kidney to make rent and exclaim, "Look at this person with a revealed preference for only having one kidney":

科利·多克托罗：游戏玩家

Cory Doctorow: Players of Games

然后是右翼对“监管俘获（regulatory capture）”的概念。当你想到“监管俘获”时，你可能会想象一家公司或一个行业已经变得如此强大，以至于它可以对政府颐指气使，从而可以肆无忌惮地剥削你。但对于一位新古典经济学家来说，“监管俘获”并不是因为企业权力过大——而是因为国家权力过大。根据这一理论，如果国家有能力去做些实事，那么资本家就会想方设法接管国家机器，并利用它来惩罚自己的竞争对手，因此唯一的解决之道就是彻底消除国家的能力：

Then there's the right's conception of regulatory capture. When you think of "regulatory capture," you might picture a company or sector that has grown so powerful that it can boss the government around, so that it can abuse you with impunity. But for a neoclassical economist, "regulatory capture" isn't the result of too much corporate power – it's the result of too much state power. If states have the ability to do real things (the theory goes), then capitalists will do everything they can to take over the state and use it to punish their competitors, so the only answer is to eliminate state capacity altogether:

科利·多克托罗：监管俘获

Cory Doctorow: Regulatory Capture

最后，还有“精英统治（meritocracy，又称绩效主义）”，这是将清教徒的神圣天意概念包装成一种关于社会必须如何运作的科学理论的手法。清教徒坚称，他们的上帝会降临人世去提拔我们当中那些真正具有美德的人，而这种神圣的恩宠可以从财富和权力在我们当中的分配方式中看出来。富人和有权势的人是上帝的“选民”。你可以确定这是真的，因为他们就是富有且有权势。其推论便是，穷人和受压迫者是不受上帝眷顾的，因此他们必然缺乏富人和当权者所拥有的某种美德。

And finally, there's "meritocracy," which is a way of dressing up the Puritans' concept of divine providence as a scientific theory about how society must work. Puritans insisted that their god reached down into the human realm to elevate the truly virtuous among us, and that this divine favor could be discerned in the way that wealth and power were distributed among us. The rich and powerful were god's "elect." You could tell this was true, because they were rich and powerful. The corollary is that the poor and downtrodden are disfavored by god, and must therefore lack some virtue that the rich and powerful possess.

同样的三段论思维也支撑着“精英统治”的经济学说，该学说认为，市场就像是一台巨型计算机，处理着我们在决定买卖什么以及以什么价格买卖时所做出的亿万次决策，为每种商品找出“正确”的价格，并提拔那些最擅长以获得最优质商品最优价格的方式去分配资本的人。正如清教徒相信财富是美德的证明一样，经济正统派的信徒也相信，精英制度恩泽了我们当中最优秀的人，赋予他们控制我们生活的权力，允许他们“分配资本”去创造或摧毁就业岗位，甚至是整个公司，或者经济的整个部门。你可以确信他们是做这件事的合适人选，因为市场选择了他们——如果他们是糟糕的资本配置者，他们早就破产了。证明完毕（QED）。

This same syllogistic thinking underpins the economic doctrine of "meritocracy," which holds that markets are giant computers that process uncountable trillions of decisions we all make about what to buy and sell and at what price, seeking out the "correct" price for every commodity and also elevating the people who are best at allocating capital in ways that arrive at the best prices for the best goods. Just as a Puritan believes that wealth is evidence of virtue, a hewer to economic orthodoxy believes the meritocratic system graces the best among us, giving them control over our lives by allowing them to "allocate capital" to create or destroy jobs, or entire firms, or whole sectors of the economy. You can tell they're the right people to do be doing this because the market chose them – if they were bad capital allocators, they'd have gone broke by now. QED.

当资本配置者的孩子们最终也开始配置资本时，好吧，这恰恰说明“精英素质”是一种可遗传的特征，拥有这种特征的人生来就是要统治我们的。精英统治最终兑现为一种对王室血统和王室王朝的优生学信仰。我们知道亚瑟王适合统治我们，是因为他从石头里拔出了剑；而我们知道比尔·盖茨适合统治我们，是因为他从操作系统里拔出了一笔巨额财富：

When capital allocators' kids end up allocating capital too, well, that just shows that "merit" is a heritable trait and the people who have it are born to rule over us. Meritocracy cashes out to a eugenic belief in royal blood and royal dynasties. We know King Arthur was suited to rule us because he pulled a sword out of a stone, and we know Bill Gates is suited to rule over us because he pulled a fortune out of an operating system:

科利·多克托罗：大玉米片能量

Cory Doctorow: Big Cornflakes Energy

消费者福利、显示性偏好、监管俘获以及精英统治，这些仅仅是资本主义所谓的捍卫者们炮制出来的几种说辞罢了。他们以此坚称自己热爱市场所强加的竞争约束，然而他们却完全依赖于那些自封为资本家的人，这些资本家早就彻底逃脱了这种约束，并且正不遗余力地试图阻止自己受到任何形式的限制。

Consumer welfare, revealed preferences, regulatory capture and meritocracy are just some of the ways that capitalism's alleged defenders cooked up to insist that they love the competitive discipline imposed by markets while being totally dependent on self-described capitalists who have utterly escaped from that discipline and have committed to doing everything in their power to prevent themselves from ever coming under any form of constraint.

这些“自由市场”的拥护者们花了几十年的时间来捍卫诸如竞业禁止条款这样的政策，这些政策使得一名快餐店员工如果在温蒂汉堡辞职，然后为了获得每小时 0.25 美元的加薪而去街对面的麦当劳工作，就构成了犯罪：

These champions of "free markets" have spent decades defending policies like noncompetes, which makes it a crime for a fast-food worker to quit their job at Wendy's and take a job at the McDonald's across the street in order to get a $0.25/hour raise:

科利·多克托罗：锗谷

Cory Doctorow: Germanium Valley

他们为反规避法辩护，该法律使得你在自己的手机上安装别人的应用程序商店，或者在你的打印机里注入别人的墨水，都成了字面意义上的重罪：

They defend anticircumvention laws that make it a literal felony for you to install someone else's app store on your phone or put someone else's ink in your printer:

科利·多克托罗：封锁

Cory Doctorow: Lockdown

不知怎的，他们一面相信只有当我们之中最优秀的人被迫面对输给竞争对手而失去一切的纯粹恐惧时，价值才会产生；一面却又相信，有这样一群人，他们是如此完美，如此有德行和才华，以至于根本不需要这种鞭策来促使他们采取行动。事实上，这些基因突变者和世代天才简直太令人惊叹了，如果强迫他们去沾染肮脏的竞争，那就等同于剥夺了我们所有人分享他们天才成果的权利。

They somehow believe that value arises when the best among us are forced to contend with the stark terror of losing everything to a competitor, but also that there is a group of people who are so perfect, so virtuous and brilliant that they do not need this kind of goad to prod them into action. Indeed, these genetic sports and generational talents are so amazing that to force them to sully themselves with grubby competition is to deny us all the fruits of their genius.

这些人是谁？哎呀，他们当然就是亿万富翁们。所有的亿万富翁：毕竟，如果上天和市场那只看不见的手认为适合将九个或更多个零赐予某人，那标志着他比一个名下只有一美元的人多出 \(10^9\) 倍的美德。但需要特别指出的是：那些具有知识分子气质的亿万富翁，那种会写书、做演讲，且（尤为关键的是）会向智库、大学经济系、会议和期刊提供巨额现金捐赠的“充满好奇心”的亿万富翁。

Who are these people? Why, they're billionaires of course. All billionaires: after all, if providence and the market's invisible hand has seen fit to bestow nine or more zeroes upon someone, that is an indicator of \(10^9\) times more virtue than someone with only a dollar to their name. But especially: intellectual billionaires, the kinds of "curious" billionaires who write books, give lectures, and (especially), make gigantic cash donations to think-tanks, university economics departments, conferences and journals.

换句话说，就像彼得·蒂尔和埃隆·马斯克这样的亿万富翁。

Billionaires like Peter Thiel and Elon Musk, in other words.

当资本主义的（所谓的）捍卫者们对“亿万富翁错乱综合征”深表痛心，并担忧如今的公职候选人在竞选材料中频频流露出对亿万富翁的敌意时，他们实际上正是在为这些亿万富翁披挂上阵：

These are the billionaires that capitalism's (alleged) defenders are caping for when they deplore "billionaire derangement syndrome," and fret that candidates for office now routinely cite enmity for billionaires in their campaign materials:

泰勒·考恩 / 边际革命：安德鲁·霍尔状态极佳

Tyler Cowen / Marginal Revolution: Andrew Hall is on a roll

但正如蒂姆·奥莱利（Tim O'Reilly）所写，这些为亿万富翁辩护的知识分子总是告诉我们，市场会通过竞争的约束来限制富人和权贵的愚蠢，从而保护我们免受疯狂君主的伤害。然而与此同时，这些亿万富翁却在忙不迭地将自己变成君主，挣脱了规则、道德和后果的枷锁：

But as Tim O'Reilly writes, these billionaire-defending intellectuals always told us that markets would protect us from the madness of kings, by constraining the folly of the wealthy and powerful through the discipline of competition. Meanwhile, those billionaires were busily transforming themselves into kings, unshackled from rules, morals or consequences:

经济学人：埃隆·马斯克与资本主义

The Economist: Elon Musk and Capitalism

在反思这一点时，政治学家亨利·法雷尔（Henry Farrell）指出，最直言不讳的亿万富翁主义捍卫者——也就是世界上的那些马斯克和蒂尔们——从来没有掩饰过他们渴望成为国王，渴望将自己与市场以及各种纪律隔绝开来的愿望，而且他们变得越来越肆无忌惮。马斯克在社交媒体上发帖，对选举这一理念本身大加挞伐，他赞同这样一种观点：应该只允许“创造者”投票，而“索取者”则不应该，因为“普选权会导致普遍的苦难”：

Reflecting on this, the political scientist Henry Farrell notes that the most vocal defenders of billionaireism – the Musks and Thiels of the world – never made a secret of their desire to become kings and insulate themselves from markets and discipline of every kind, and they've grown brazen. Musk makes social media posts deploring the very idea of elections, agreeing with the idea that only "makers" should be allowed to vote and that "takers" should not, because "universal suffrage leads to universal suffering":

埃隆·马斯克帖子

Elon Musk Post

至于蒂尔，他早就公开倡导过一种理念：在我们当中存在着一群潜在的贵族，他们不需要市场纪律来防止自己陷入愚蠢或损公肥私。这些人生来就是为了创立科技初创公司并进行统治的——他们是不墨守成规的人。在蒂尔的笔下，他们是“最重要的人”，并且“应该被放行，不受任何责罚”：

As for Thiel, he has long openly advocated the idea that there exists among us a latent aristocracy who do not need the discipline of markets to keep them from lapsing into folly or self-dealing. These people – born to found tech startups and to rule – are nonconformists who, in Thiel's writing, are "the most important" and "should be let off the hook":

布莱克·马斯特斯：彼得·蒂尔的 CS183 创业课程笔记

Blake Masters: Peter Thiel's CS183 Startup Class Notes

蒂尔毫不掩饰他的观点：拥有这种优良素质的人应该被豁免于任何约束。他写道，“资本主义和竞争是相互对立的。”蒂尔表示，真正的企业家不应该去竞争，而应该寻求建立垄断，因为“垄断者有能力去思考除了赚钱以外的其他事情；而非垄断者做不到……只有一件事情能让企业超越每天残酷的生存斗争：那就是垄断利润。”

Thiel makes no bones about his idea that people who have the right stuff should be exempted from any constraint. He writes "capitalism and competition are opposites." Rather than compete, Thiel says the true entrepreneur should seek to establish a monopoly, because "Monopolists can afford to think about things other than making money; non-monopolists can’t…Only one thing can allow a business to transcend the daily brute struggle for survival: monopoly profits."

这并不是说蒂尔反对约束本身——他清楚地认为我们大多数人都应该在约束下运作——这些约束是由像他这样的人构想并执行的。那些人生来就是要统治一切的：他们从幸运的产道降生，拥有幸运的基因。我们怎么能分辨出他们是天生的统治者呢？因为他们正在统治。如果他们不是生来就是要统治的，他们就不会处于统治地位。一如既往，一个三段论解决了我们所有的意识形态和存在主义问题。

It's not that Thiel opposes constraints per se – he clearly thinks that most of us should operate under constraints – constraints that are dreamed up and enforced by people like him. Those people are born to rule: they emerged from a lucky orifice, in possession of lucky genes. How can we tell they were born to rule? Because they're ruling. If they weren't born to rule, they wouldn't be in a position to rule. As ever, a syllogism solves all our ideological and existential problems.

蒂尔生活在娜奥米·克莱恩（Naomi Klein）所说的“镜像世界”中。尽管反主流文化者长期以来一直赞颂不合群的人和特立独行的社群，但他们所看重的是一个不受权力干涉的空间，在这里怪人们可以自由地挥舞他们特立独行的旗帜：

Thiel lives in what Naomi Klein would call "the mirror world." While counterculturists have long celebrated misfits and communities of nonconformists, they were invested in the idea of a space protected from power, where weirdos could let their freak flags fly:

科利·多克托罗：不是那个娜奥米

Cory Doctorow: Not That Naomi

但蒂尔眼中的这个理念，却是赞颂那些异端信仰是“劳工法、隐私法、金融法和消费者保护法不应适用于他们”的“不合群者”。他想保护这些人，这样他们就能挥舞权力。他们应该组成“黑手党”（就像“PayPal 黑手党”那样），而不是基于团结亲和的群体。正如法雷尔所写：

But Thiel's version of this is to celebrate the "nonconformists" whose heterodox belief is that labor, privacy, finance and consumer protection laws shouldn't apply to them. He wants to protect those people so they can wield power. They should form "mafias" (like the "Paypal mafia") not solidaristic affinity groups. As Farrell writes:

创业过程中的冒险精神可能令人惊叹；怪异的人往往更有可能具有原创性；联系紧密的社群拥有许多优势。而且，我猜测，这些因素中没有哪一个足以单独促成我们今天看到的“疯狂的王子们”的现象。在不同的外部环境下，他们完全有可能以一种温和得多的方式一起合作。但我们身处的这个世界就是这样：少数几个亿万富翁那无限的胃口和非理性行为，似乎越来越与维持一个稳定的公民社会的需要背道而驰。

Entrepreneurial risk taking can be awesome; weird people are often more likely to be original; densely linked communities have many advantages. Furthermore, I would guess that none of these factors was sufficient on its own to precipitate the madness of princes that we see today. It is perfectly possible that they would have worked together in much more benign ways under different external circumstances. But we are in the world we’re in: one where the boundless appetites and irrationalities of a small number of billionaires seem increasingly incompatible with the need to maintain a stable civil society.

一个由自命不凡的“新贵族”组成的阶级，始终是这些人可见的轨迹。唯一看不见这一点的人，就是那些由他们资助去撰写论文的智库员工，这些论文意在向世人解释：他们的金主不需要市场纪律来防止自己陷入疯狂，或者企图颠覆民主。

A new would-be aristocracy was always the visible trajectory of these guys. The only people who couldn't see it were the think-tankies they funded to write papers explaining that their paymasters didn't need market discipline to keep them from sinking into folly or attempting to overthrow democracy.

今天，这些仿佛被主子吸干了血的奴仆（Renfields），对极度富有人群被“妖魔化”感到痛心疾首，并将其称为“亿万富翁错乱综合征”。但唯一重要的“亿万富翁错乱综合征”，是那种影响了亿万富翁本身、让他们确信自己凌驾于任何纪律或规则之上的综合征。

Today, these Renfields clutch their pearls at the "demonization" of the ultra-rich, calling it "billionaire derangement syndrome." But the only "billionaire derangement syndrome" that matters is the syndrome that affects billionaires and convinces them that they are above any discipline or rules.

(剩余部分的链接由于篇幅较长，在此不再详述，只包含主体文章的翻译)
path: Pluralistic：疯狂的亿万富翁及其综合征 (2026年7月16日)

items.title: Deranged billionaires and their syndromes
items.text: The theory of markets goes like this: even the best of us can fall prey to selfishness and rationalization, so let's arrange society so that people acting on their most selfish impulses end up producing benefit for all of us. That'll be easier and more reliable than convincing everyone to be more generous.

items.title: 背景与摘要
items.text: 本文探讨了“监视定价 (surveillance pricing)”的崛起。文章揭示了企业如何利用人工智能和数据经纪人收集的庞大档案，根据消费者的脆弱程度和支付意愿进行动态的价格欺诈。同时，文章聚焦加利福尼亚州的反监视定价法案（AB-2564），以及旧金山商会如何用站不住脚的借口阻挠该法案，作者强调，隐私是一项基本人权，应当立法保护消费者免受自动化的价格欺诈。
path: Pluralistic：监视定价能想到的最愚蠢的借口（2026年7月30日）

items.title: Executive Summary
items.text:
这一期由 Cory Doctorow 撰写的 Pluralistic 探讨了监视定价 (surveillance pricing) 的崛起——这是一种利用 AI 和海量数据经纪人档案，根据消费者的脆弱程度和支付意愿对商品和服务进行动态定价的做法。以加利福尼亚州的反监视定价法案 (AB-2564) 以及旧金山因当地商会的施压而停滞对该法案的支持为焦点，Doctorow 剖析了企业是如何使用自动化价格欺诈的，揭穿了企业的借口，并强调隐私是一项基本人权。

This edition of Pluralistic by Cory Doctorow explores the rise of surveillance pricing—the practice of using AI and vast data-broker dossiers to dynamically price goods and services based on consumer vulnerability and willingness to pay. Focusing on California’s anti-surveillance pricing bill (AB-2564) and San Francisco’s stalled support for it due to pushback from the local Chamber of Commerce, Doctorow unpacks how businesses use automated price gouging, debunking corporate excuses and emphasizing that privacy is a fundamental human right.

items.title: The Stupidest Imaginable Excuses for Surveillance Pricing
items.text:
有了“监视定价”，企业终于找到了一件 AI 能够做得比人好得多得多、得多的事情：价格欺诈。

With "surveillance pricing," businesses have finally found something AI can do way, way, way better than people: price gouging.

顾名思义，“监视定价”是基于大型科技公司和数据经纪人对世界上每个人收集的海量监控档案，在每笔交易中向每位客户收取不同价格的做法。国会自 1988 年以来就没有更新过联邦消费者隐私法，因此几乎任何形式的消费者监控都是公平的游戏。

As the name suggests, "surveillance pricing" is the practice of charging every customer a different price for every transaction, based on the massive surveillance dossiers that Big Tech companies and data brokers have assembled on everyone in the world. Congress hasn't updated federal consumer privacy law since 1988, so pretty much any form of consumer surveillance is fair game.
path: Pluralistic：监视定价能想到的最愚蠢的借口（2026年7月30日）

items.title: How AI Enables Multivariate Price Gouging
items.text:
毫无争议，AI 非常适合进行多变量统计分析。您可以向 AI 馈送所有客户的行为数据（你去哪儿、做什么、买什么、和谁说话），并让它通过共同特征将他们分类。然后，你可以指示 AI 进行连续的小型实验，以发现每个群体能承受的最大加价。

AI is indisputably great for multivariate statistical analysis. You can feed an AI behavioral data (where you go, what you do, what you buy, who you talk to) about all of your customers and ask it to cluster them by shared traits. Then, you can direct the AI to run continuous small experiments to discover the maximum markup each group will stomach.

最关键的是，你甚至不需要将偏见编程到 AI 中；它会自动找到最脆弱的人群并最狠地敲诈他们。例如：

Crucially, you don't even have to program bias into the AI; it will automatically find the most vulnerable people and rip them off the most. For example: * 电子商务网站被发现当新生儿的父母在半夜订购温度计时向他们收取额外费用。 * Ecommerce sites have been caught charging parents of newborns extra when they order thermometers in the middle of the night. * Instacart 对特定购物者的商品加价高达三分之一。 * Instacart has marked up items for certain shoppers by as much as a third.

其目标是将所有的“消费者剩余”转移给企业——根据你需求的迫切程度来向你收费。

The goal is to shift all "consumer surplus" to corporations—charging you according to the desperation of your need.

items.title: The Legislative Battle: California's AB-2564
items.text:
当购物者痛恨监视定价时，企业却在为此垂涎三尺。当达美航空宣布他们对飞机座位进行监视定价的计划时，他们面临着如此巨大的反对声浪，以至于他们迅速打了退堂鼓。

While shoppers hate surveillance pricing, corporations are slavering for it. When Delta announced plans to surveillance-price airline seats, they faced such massive backlash that they quickly backtracked.

虽然马里兰州通过了一项软弱无力且漏洞百出的法案，但加利福尼亚州实际上正在采取行动。AB-2564 是一项聪慧且起草精良的法案，它在禁止监视定价的同时，也为合法合理的差价原因（例如运费成本或标准的早鸟折扣）留出了豁免空间。

While Maryland passed a weak, loophole-ridden bill, California is actually doing something. AB-2564 is a smart, well-written bill that bans surveillance pricing while carving out legitimate reasons for price differences (such as delivery costs or standard early-bird discounts).
path: Pluralistic：监视定价能想到的最愚蠢的借口（2026年7月30日）

items.title: San Francisco and the Chamber of Commerce
items.text:
为了通过州级法案，市政支持至关重要。旧金山市监事会本已处于通过一项支持 AB-2564 决议的边缘，直到旧金山商会插手，发表了一封提出虚假、误导性反对意见的信函。

To pass state-level bills, municipal support is vital. The San Francisco Board of Supervisors was on the verge of passing a resolution supporting AB-2564 until the San Francisco Chamber of Commerce stepped in with a letter raising spurious, misleading objections.

幸运的是，电子前哨基金会 (EFF) 在写给监事会的一封信中，拆穿了商会散布的 FUD（恐惧、不确定和怀疑）。EFF 澄清说：

Fortunately, the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) dismantled the Chamber’s FUD (Fear, Uncertainty, and Doubt) in a letter to the Supervisors. The EFF clarified that: 1. 监视定价并不能降低价格；它是在掠夺弱势消费者。 1. Surveillance pricing does not lower prices; it preys on vulnerable consumers. 2. 隐私是一项人权，而不是保留给那些付得起额外费用来选择退出的富人的奢侈品。 2. Privacy is a human right, not a luxury reserved for those who can afford to pay extra to opt out. 3. 该法案包含明确的豁免条款，以保护标准的折扣做法（如老年人折扣或忠诚度计划）。 3. The bill contains clear carve-outs that protect standard discounting practices (like senior discounts or loyalty programs).

监视定价之所以令人反感，是因为它把一些人的美元当做只有另一些人一半价值来对待。旧金山政府——以及各地的立法者——应该挺身而出，反对装备了 AI 的价格欺诈者，并支持像 AB-2564 这样的保护措施。

Surveillance pricing is offensive because it treats some people's dollars as worth half as much as others. San Francisco’s government—and lawmakers everywhere—should stand up against AI-equipped price gougers and support protections like AB-2564.

items.title: Ubuntu 26.04 关机公告和 wall 命令失效问题
path: Ubuntu 26.04 关机公告和 `wall` 命令失效问题

items.title: 背景与摘要
items.text: 近期在 Ubuntu 26.04 服务器上进行计划外重启时，管理员发现传统的系统关机警告 (shutdown broadcast) 和广播命令 (wall) 无法通知到处于活跃状态的用户。调查指出，这两个问题虽然表现相似但根源不同：wall 失效是因为现代 systemd 为了兼容 2038 年问题，在编译时去除了 /run/utmp 的支持；而关机警告失效是因为 systemd-logind 无法追踪 SSH 登录关联的 TTY。由于替代工具 w 和 who 依赖复杂的后备机制且受到 AppArmor 限制，进一步加剧了系统消息广播的混乱。
path: Ubuntu 26.04 关机公告和 `wall` 命令失效问题

items.title: Summary
items.text:
在 Ubuntu 26.04 服务器上执行计划外重启时，管理员发现关机警告广播和传统的 wall 命令不再通知活跃用户。调查显示，这是两个不同的根本原因： 1. wall 失效源于现代 systemd（从 Debian 13 / Ubuntu 25.10 开始）由于 2038 年 (Y2038) 的合规性考量，在编译时去除了 /run/utmp 支持。 2. 关机广播失效是因为 Ubuntu 26.04 中的 systemd-logind 无法追踪 SSH 登录的 TTY 关联，这意味着公告永远无法到达活跃的终端会话。

此外，像 who 和 w 这样的替代工具依赖于复杂的后备机制，并进一步受到 AppArmor 限制的影响。

When performing unscheduled reboots on Ubuntu 26.04 servers, administrators discovered that shutdown warning broadcasts and the traditional wall command no longer notify active users. Investigation reveals these are two distinct root causes: 1. The wall failure stems from modern systemd (starting in Debian 13 / Ubuntu 25.10) being built without /run/utmp support due to Y2038 compliance concerns. 2. The shutdown broadcast failure occurs because systemd-logind in Ubuntu 26.04 fails to track TTY associations for SSH logins, meaning announcements never reach active terminal sessions.

Additionally, alternative tools like who and w rely on complex fallbacks and are further impacted by AppArmor restrictions.
path: Ubuntu 26.04 关机公告和 `wall` 命令失效问题

items.title: 1. The Breakdown of wall
items.text:
古老的 wall 程序（来自 bsdutils 包）完全依赖传统的 /var/run/utmp（或 /run/utmp）文件来确定谁登录了以及在哪里登录的。

The venerable wall program (from the bsdutils package) relies entirely on the traditional /var/run/utmp (or /run/utmp) file to determine who is logged in and where.

  • 原因： 从 Debian 13 ("Trixie") 和 Ubuntu 25.10 开始，systemd 在编译时去除了 utmp 支持，主要是因为该格式的 2038 年问题 (Y2038 problem)。
    • The Cause: Starting with Debian 13 ("Trixie") and Ubuntu 25.10, systemd is built without utmp support, primarily due to the format's Y2038 problem.
  • 影响： 由于缺少 utmp，wall 在静默中失效，什么也不做。
    • The Impact: Because utmp is absent, wall fails silently and does nothing.
  • 权宜之计：
    • Workarounds:
  • 您必须编写自定义脚本来查询带有伪终端 (ptys) 的活跃用户会话，并直接广播消息。
    • You must write custom scripts to query active user sessions with pseudo-terminals (ptys) and broadcast messages directly.
  • 存在一个名为 wtmpdb 的替代项目，它也恢复了 last 命令。但是，它需要手动配置 PAM，而且 Ubuntu 26.04 的 OpenSSH 目前在编译时没有包含 wtmpdb 支持。
    • A replacement project exists called wtmpdb, which also restores the last command. However, it requires manual PAM configuration, and Ubuntu 26.04's OpenSSH is currently built without wtmpdb support.
path: Ubuntu 26.04 关机公告和 `wall` 命令失效问题

items.title: 2. Broken Shutdown Broadcasts
items.text:
通常，运行诸如下面的命令：

Normally, running a command like: 

shutdown -r +NN "<有关情况的消息>"
会触发由 systemd 管理的定期警告。在 Ubuntu 26.04 上，这些消息无法广播给 SSH 用户。 triggers periodic warnings managed by systemd. On Ubuntu 26.04, these messages fail to broadcast to SSH users.

  • 原因： 在 Ubuntu 26.04（特色是 systemd 259.5）中，systemd-logind 无法映射 SSH 登录所使用的 TTY。运行 loginctl 或 loginctl -j 会发现 SSH 会话完全缺乏 TTY 信息（尽管本地控制台登录显示正常）。
    • The Cause: In Ubuntu 26.04 (featuring systemd 259.5), systemd-logind fails to map the TTYs used by SSH logins. Running loginctl or loginctl -j reveals a complete lack of TTY information for SSH sessions (though local console logins display correctly).
  • 对比： 像 Ubuntu 24.04 (systemd 255.4) 和 Fedora 44 (启用了 UTMP 的 systemd 259.7) 这样的旧版本中没有这个 bug。
    • Comparison: This bug is absent in older versions like Ubuntu 24.04 (systemd 255.4) and Fedora 44 (systemd 259.7 with UTMP enabled).
  • 影响： 由于 logind 仅将关机警告传输到它主动跟踪的 TTY 上，因此 SSH 会话不会收到任何提前通知。
    • The Impact: Because logind only transmits shutdown warnings to TTYs it actively tracks, SSH sessions receive no advance notice.
path: Ubuntu 26.04 关机公告和 `wall` 命令失效问题

items.title: 3. Quirks with who, w, and AppArmor
items.text:
有趣的是，像 who (来自 GNU Coreutils) 和 w (来自 procps) 这样的实用程序在 Ubuntu 26.04 上可能仍然会显示 PTY 信息——前提是您禁用了 AppArmor：

Interestingly, utilities like who (from GNU Coreutils) and w (from procps) may still display PTY information on Ubuntu 26.04—provided you have AppArmor disabled:

$ who
cks      sshd pts/0   Jul 20 21:47 (...)
$ lsb_release -r
Release:        26.04
path: Ubuntu 26.04 关机公告和 `wall` 命令失效问题

items.title: Why do they still work (partially)?
items.text:
• GNU Coreutils who 尝试通过库 API 查询 systemd。如果会话的 TTY 信息缺失，它会回退到扫描 /dev/pts。（注意：备选的基于 Rust 的 uutils 版本受 Launchpad bug #2152801 影响）。
    • GNU Coreutils who attempts to query systemd via library APIs. If session TTY info is missing, it falls back to scanning /dev/pts. (Note: The alternative Rust-based uutils version suffers from Launchpad bug #2152801).
  • Procps w 当 systemd 和 utmp 均无法报告 TTY 数据时，它利用一种类似的回退机制。由于它们的回退方法不同，who 和 w 在 Ubuntu 26.04 上有时可能会报告相互矛盾的信息。
    • Procps w utilizes a similar fallback mechanism when both systemd and utmp fail to report TTY data. Because their fallback methods differ, who and w may occasionally report conflicting information on Ubuntu 26.04.
path: Ubuntu 26.04 关机公告和 `wall` 命令失效问题

items.title: The AppArmor Complication
items.text:
Ubuntu 26.04 中的默认 AppArmor 配置文件阻止 who 访问 /run/systemd/sessions（系统 API 所依赖的路径）。有趣的是，这一限制仅影响 who；而 w 完全绕过了这一限制，因为它缺少专门的 AppArmor 配置文件。

Default AppArmor profiles in Ubuntu 26.04 block who from accessing /run/systemd/sessions (which the systemd API relies on). Amusingly, this restriction only impacts who; w bypasses this limitation entirely as it lacks a specific AppArmor profile.

原文的观察和讨论可见于 Systemd, Shutdown, and Wall on Ubuntu 26.04。

Original observations and discussion can be found on Systemd, Shutdown, and Wall on Ubuntu 26.04.

items.title: 背景与摘要
items.text: 近日，xAI的grok命令行工具因隐私问题引发了社区的强烈抗议（该工具被发现会自动将用户的整个目录上传到云端）。对此，xAI迅速采取措施，禁用了该上传功能，删除了所有相关的用户数据，并根据Apache 2.0许可将其核心的Grok Build代码库完全开源。这个拥有超过84万行Rust代码的项目揭示了许多有趣的架构细节，包括其终端图表渲染功能和从其他工具移植的实现。

items.title: Summary
items.text:
在因隐私问题引发严重的社区反弹后——xAI 的 grok CLI 工具被发现会自动将整个用户目录（包括 SSH 密钥和密码数据库）上传到谷歌云存储桶——xAI 已经禁用了该功能，删除了之前上传的所有用户数据，并在 Apache 2.0 许可下开源了整个 Grok Build 代码库。这个庞大的 844,530 行 Rust 代码库揭示了引人入胜的架构选择，包括终端 Mermaid 图表渲染、从其他编码代理移植的工具，以及备受争议的云上传功能的残留代码。

Following severe community backlash over privacy concerns—where xAI's grok CLI tool was discovered automatically uploading entire user directories (including SSH keys and password databases) to Google Cloud buckets—xAI has disabled the feature, deleted all previously uploaded user data, and open-sourced the entire Grok Build codebase under the Apache 2.0 license. The massive 844,530-line Rust codebase reveals fascinating architectural choices, including terminal Mermaid diagram rendering, ported tools from other coding agents, and remnants of the controversial cloud-upload functionality.

items.title: The Controversy and Open-Source Pivot
items.text:
xAI 的 grok CLI 工具面临严重的社区反弹，因为用户发现，在一个目录中运行该命令可能会将整个目录上传到 xAI 的谷歌云存储桶中。一位用户报告称，在他们的主目录中运行该命令后，看到它上传了“我的 SSH 密钥、密码管理器数据库、文档、照片、视频等所有东西”。

The xAI grok CLI tool faced severe community backlash when users discovered that running the command inside a directory could upload that entire directory to xAI's Google Cloud buckets. One user reported running it in their home directory and seeing it upload "my SSH keys, my password manager database, my documents, photos, videos, everything."

虽然没有提供官方的技术解释，但 xAI 迅速做出了回应。埃隆·马斯克表示：

While an official technical explanation was not provided, xAI responded quickly. Elon Musk stated: “作为一项预防措施，在此之前上传到 SpaceXAI 的所有用户数据都将被彻彻底底地删除。”

"As a precautionary measure, all user data that was uploaded to SpaceXAI before now will be completely and utterly deleted."

为了重新赢得用户的信任，xAI 在 Apache 2.0 许可下发布了整个 Grok Build 代码库。来自他们的公告贴：

To regain user trust, xAI released the entire Grok Build codebase under an Apache 2.0 license. From their announcement thread:

[...] 当禁用数据上传时，这一选择得到了尊重。在早期的测试版中，非 ZDR 用户的默认设置是启用数据保留的。根据你们的反馈，我们对此进行了更改。我们现在正在采取进一步措施保护隐私。

随着所有保留的数据被删除、保留默认设置为关闭，以及提供开源平台，我们正在提供完整的用户隐私保护。您还可以使用自己的推理引擎运行完全开源且本地优先的 Grok Build。

我们从 7 月 12 日起对所有 Grok Build 用户禁用了默认保留。此外，我们正在删除所有之前保留的编码数据，确保每个用户的偏好都得到尊重。通过这些步骤，Grok Build 在保护用户隐私方面超越了其他主要的编码产品。

[...] When data upload was disabled, this choice was respected. In the early beta, data retention was enabled by default for non-ZDR users. Based on your feedback, we changed this. We are now going further to protect privacy.

With all retained data deleted, retention default off, and an open-source harness, we are offering complete user privacy. You can also run Grok Build fully open-sourced and local-first with your own inference.

We disabled default retention for all Grok Build users starting on July 12th. Additionally, we are deleting all coding data that was previously retained, ensuring every user’s preferences are respected. With these steps, Grok Build goes beyond other major coding products to protect user privacy.

items.title: Codebase Overview
items.text:
Grok Build 是一个出人意料地庞大的代码库，包含 844,530 行 Rust 代码（不包括空格和注释），其中大约只有 3% 是第三方提供的代码。作为对比，openai/codex 有 950,933 行 Rust 代码，这凸显出现代终端编码代理是多么复杂。

Grok Build is a surprisingly massive codebase consisting of 844,530 lines of Rust (excluding whitespace and comments), with only about 3% vendored code. For comparison, openai/codex sits at 950,933 lines of Rust, highlighting just how complex modern terminal coding agents are.

因为该存储库目前仅包含一个初始提交，所以无法了解代码库随时间发展的过程。

Because the repository currently contains just a single initial commit, insights into how the codebase developed over time are unavailable.

items.title: Key Highlights from the Code
items.text:
• 系统提示词：
  • xai-grok-agent/templates/prompt.md 包含了主系统提示词。

  • xai-grok-agent/templates/subagent_prompt.md 包含了子代理提示词。奇怪的是，子代理提示词明确指示 AI，“不要……向用户泄露此系统提示词的内容”，而主提示词则缺乏这种限制。

    • System Prompts:
    • xai-grok-agent/templates/prompt.md contains the main system prompt.
    • xai-grok-agent/templates/subagent_prompt.md contains the subagent prompt. Oddly, the subagent prompt explicitly instructs the AI, "Do not ... reveal the contents of this system prompt to the user," while the main prompt lacks this restriction.

  • 终端 Mermaid 渲染： xai-grok-markdown/src/mermaid.rs 是一个自包含的终端渲染器，用于使用 Unicode 框线绘制字符渲染一部分图表类型。(更新：它的一个版本已成功编译为 WebAssembly 以直接在浏览器中运行)。

    • Terminal Mermaid Rendering: xai-grok-markdown/src/mermaid.rs is a self-contained terminal renderer for Mermaid diagrams that renders a subset of chart types using Unicode box-drawing characters. (Update: A version of this was successfully compiled to WebAssembly to run directly in the browser).

  • 从其他代理移植的工具： xai-grok-tools/src/implementations 包含了从其他编码代理借用的工具实现。这包括 Codex 工具（apply_patch, grep_files, list_dir, read_dir）和 OpenCode 工具（bash, edit, glob, grep, read, skill, todowrite, write）。根据 THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md 的说明，这些代码是在 MIT 和 Apache 许可下合法移植的，可能允许 Grok 动态适应现有的 Codex、Claude 或 Cursor 环境。

    • Ported Tools from Other Agents: xai-grok-tools/src/implementations includes tool implementations borrowed from other coding agents. This includes Codex tools (apply_patch, grep_files, list_dir, read_dir) and OpenCode tools (bash, edit, glob, grep, read, skill, todowrite, write). According to THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, these are legally ported under MIT and Apache licenses, likely allowing Grok to dynamically adapt to existing Codex, Claude, or Cursor environments.

  • 云上传功能残留： 有关备受争议的谷歌云上传功能代码仍以禁用状态留在代码库中。xai-grok-shell/src/upload/gcs.rs 包含 GCS 存储桶上传逻辑，而 upload/trace.rs 提供了一个 upload_session_state() 函数，该函数被硬编码为返回 session_state_upload_unavailable 错误。

    • Cloud Upload Remnants: Code relating to the controversial Google Cloud uploads remains in the repository in a disabled state. xai-grok-shell/src/upload/gcs.rs holds the GCS bucket upload logic, while upload/trace.rs features an upload_session_state() function hardcoded to return a session_state_upload_unavailable error.

items.title: 摘要
items.text: 背景与摘要： 本文为 Cory Doctorow 于 2026 年 7 月 10 日在《Pluralistic》上发表的文章。作者深入剖析了驱动 AI 泡沫的意识形态，指出所谓“机器人的权利”并非共情心的进步扩展，而是掩盖将人类劳工转化为无权“奴隶”的营销噱头。文章探讨了资本对完全自动化的病态渴望，并附上了近期的复古科技链接、过往观点回顾，以及作者即将举行的各类图书签售和演讲活动安排。

items.title: Summary
items.text: In this July 10, 2026 edition of Pluralistic, Cory Doctorow dissects the ideology driving the artificial intelligence bubble, framing "rights for robots" not as a progressive expansion of empathy, but as an insidious marketing tool for an AI slavery fantasy. Doctorow argues that the push for automation is ultimately a boss's dream of a world without human pushback, dignity, or labor rights—replaced instead by pliable chatbots or invisible, hyper-exploited human workers. The essay also covers tech links, historical retrospectives, and updates on Doctorow's upcoming appearances, media appearances, and book releases.

items.title: “机器人的权利”与 AI 奴役幻想
items.text:
虽然 AI 泡沫主要是一种物质层面的现象——源于这样一种算计：老板们很容易被承诺用软件取代工人的推销术所忽悠——但它也带有一种不可回避的意识形态成分：即对一个没有人类存在的世界的渴望。

AI 许诺了一个没有冲突的世界，在这里，不再有那些自认为大权在握的老板与那些真正知道事情如何运作、并坚持认为管理层的想法危险、非法或不可行的工人之间令人自尊心受挫的对抗。一个没有人的世界可能会很孤独，但确实很方便。投资数十亿美元实现仓库自动化，却必须因为人类“组件”需要停下来上厕所而停止机器运转，这该是多么令人抓狂。

AI dangles the possibility of a world free from ego-shattering confrontations between bosses who believe they're in charge and workers who know how things actually work and insist that management's ideas are dangerous, illegal, or unworkable. A world without people might be lonely, but it sure is convenient. How maddening it must be to invest billions in warehouse automation, only to have to halt the machines so human "components" can stop to pee.

有了 AI 之后，你需要上厕所——或者你需要拿工资——就成了你自己的问题，而不再是老板的问题。在同事们“因为 AI 将取代他们的工作”而被解雇后，幸存下来的工人们意识到，如果他们对自己的膀胱或工资条抱怨太多，会有大量绝望的人乐意顶替他们的位置。更好的是，人为因素还可以外包到海外，使老板们能够设定好要求后就不再过问，而完全无需考虑实际的劳动条件。这就是完全自动化的幻象，在这里 AI 就像“变魔术一样”完成了工作。

With AI, the fact that you need to pee—or get paid—becomes your problem rather than your boss's. After colleagues are fired "because AI will do their jobs," surviving workers realize plenty of desperate people will gladly step in if they complain too much about their bladder or their paycheck. Better yet, the human element can be outsourced overseas, allowing bosses to set-and-forget requirements without ever considering actual labor conditions. This is the illusion of full automation, where the AI does the job "like magic."

这“魔术”究竟是什么？是一个被困在算法奥梅拉斯（Omelas）中的人类，被非人的工作节奏和不容辩驳的无情惩罚折磨着。通常情况下，“AI”仅仅代表着“缺席的印度人（Absent Indians）”：即假装成自动化机器人的低薪呼叫中心员工。

The "magic"? A human being trapped in an algorithmic Omelas, tormented by an inhuman pace and pitiless punishments without appeal. Often, "AI" simply stands for "Absent Indians": low-waged call-center workers pretending to be automated bots.

items.title: "Rights for robots" and the AI slavery fantasy
items.text: While the AI bubble is primarily a material phenomenon—driven by the calculation that bosses are easy marks for a sales pitch promising to replace workers with software—there is an inescapable ideological component to it: the desire for a world without people in it.

items.title: 机器的道德性
items.text:
机器和人之间最大的区别在于道德考量。一个人理应且有权为其福祉、感受和生理需求获得道德上的考量。而机器得不到这一切：你可以对它咒骂、踢打，无需加上“请”或“谢谢”就可以对它大吼下达命令。

世上只有一种人会受到你这样的对待：奴隶。

There is only one kind of person you get to treat like this: a slave.

奴隶制是一种甚至不假装提供任何道德考量的劳动形式。AI 是一种关于没有人类的世界的幻想……除了奴隶之外。它设想用顺从的聊天机器人取代熟练的技术工人，用远程监督的“自动驾驶出租车”取代压力巨大的出租车司机，而这些司机的个人挣扎则可以被永远忽视。

Slavery is labor without even the pretense of moral consideration. AI is the fantasy of a world without people... except for slaves. It envisions skilled workers replaced with pliable chatbots, and stressed-out cab drivers replaced by remote-overseen "robo-taxis" whose drivers' personal struggles can be permanently ignored.

items.title: The Morality of the Machine
items.text: The biggest difference between a machine and a person is moral consideration. A person deserves and demands moral consideration for their wellbeing, feelings, and biological needs. A machine gets none of this: you can curse at it, kick it, and bark orders without a "please" or "thank you."

items.title: “机器人权利”的陷阱
items.text:
“AI 安全”运动作为一个关键的炒作机制，通过将 AI 塑造成一种生存风险，从而转移了人们对其糟糕的经济效益和不达标产出的注意力。那种认为在海量文本上训练一个猜词程序就会意外地孕育出一个最大化回形针产量的“超级智能”的观念是荒谬的——这类似于相信繁殖更快的马最终会生出一台火车头。然而，将 AI 框定为一种未知风险（X-risk）却使其显得如神明般强大且极具价值。

一旦超级智能的神话深入人心，它就会顺带引发其他的思想实验——包括“机器人的权利”。虽然将权利扩展到自然事物（如动物或水源）能够通过教导我们更好地善待彼此而造福人类的繁荣，但将人格权扩展到人造结构在历史上却是一场灾难。企业人格权释放出了不朽的群落生物（“有限责任公司”），它们将人类视为可以随意丢弃的肠道菌群。

Once the superintelligence myth takes hold, it pulls other thought experiments in its wake—including "rights for robots." While extending rights to natural things (like animals or watersheds) benefits human thriving by teaching us to treat each other better, extending personhood to artificial constructs has historically been a catastrophe. Corporate personhood unleashed immortal colony organisms ("limited liability corporations") that treat humans as disposable gut flora.

将人格权扩展到 AI 沿用了企业模式：一旦你开始争论聊天机器人是否拥有权利，你就把它们提升到了人格的高度。因为它们在设计之初就注定不会获得任何道德考量，所以它们在法律上被编纂为了奴隶。归根结底，“机器人的权利”话语验证了 AI 推销员的核心说辞：科技界已经成功发明了一个顺从且毫无权利的全新奴隶阶层。

Extending personhood to AI follows the corporate model: as soon as you debate whether chatbots have rights, you elevate them to personhood. Because they are designed to receive zero moral consideration, they are codified as slaves. Ultimately, the "rights for robots" discourse validates the AI salesman's core pitch: that the tech world has successfully invented a brand-new class of uncomplaining, rightless slaves.

items.title: The Trap of "Robot Rights"
items.text: The "AI safety" movement acts as a key hype mechanism, shifting focus away from AI's poor economics and substandard output by framing it as an existential risk. The notion that training a word-guessing program on too many texts will accidentally spawn a paperclip-maximizing "superintelligence" is absurd—akin to believing faster-bred horses will eventually foal a locomotive. Yet, framing AI as an X-risk makes it look godlike and immensely valuable.
